question: Does PTSM retain probability-level information when discrete argmax transition delay is held fixed?

transition_unit.primary_event_ptsm: mean max(p_old - p_new, 0) over the eligible post-transition window
transition_unit.delay: first argmax prediction of the new class; a miss is coded as the horizon
transition_unit.primary_equal_delay_subset: paired events at horizon 16 where raw and EMA 0.50 have the same detected delay in 0..15
transition_unit.missed_events: excluded from the primary equal-delay test because delay=16 is right-censored; included as a named sensitivity subset

primary_test.estimand: event-weighted mean paired PTSM difference, EMA 0.50 minus raw, among exactly equal detected-delay events
primary_test.pass_rule: lower endpoint of the paired video-cluster 95% percentile CI is above zero

bounded_sensitivity_checks.transition_type_pass_rule: PTSM difference CI is above zero for at least two types with at least 100 events
bounded_sensitivity_checks.horizon_pass_rule: all three PTSM difference CIs are above zero
bounded_sensitivity_checks.ece_pass_rule: all global-ECE difference CIs are below zero
bounded_sensitivity_checks.individual_delay_strata: descriptive only; no single selected stratum may carry the gate

overall_gate: primary equal-delay test passes, at least two transition types pass, all horizon directions pass, and all ECE-bin directions pass
failure_action: If the primary equal-delay test fails, PTSM is downgraded to a descriptive probability statistic. No revised metric may be invented. Other ranking-inversion claims remain evaluated independently.
anti_p_hacking_rules: the pooled exact-delay subset is the only primary nonredundancy test
individual delay strata are descriptive and may not replace the pooled test
alpha 0.25 may be reported as sensitivity but may not rescue a failed alpha 0.50 primary test
horizons and ECE bin counts are fixed before analysis
resampling is paired by video, never by transition or frame
